hypothesis: The failed int7 STE arms optimized 129600 continuous masters even though the browser stores only fixed codes and per-output scales. Freezing every signed-int7 code and training only the 240 deployed FP16 scales should produce lower-variance recovery while preserving model size and kernel behavior.

primary_arm.name: mask7-fixed-codes-scales-only
primary_arm.meaning: Lloyd codes and scales on RSTB fusion stages 0, 1, and 2; max-range on stage 3
primary_arm.frozen_values: all int7 codes, all ternary weights, all FP16 weight islands, biases, and non-scale parameters

early_gate.step_250: At least one live metric must improve and neither ground-truth nor teacher PSNR may fall more than 0.002 dB from the exact step-zero baseline.
early_gate.step_500: Both live ground-truth and teacher PSNR must be nonnegative versus step zero; otherwise stop the arm.
early_gate.fallback: If mask 7 fails, run the identical scale-only arm from max-range mask 0. If both fail, reduce the learning rate to 0.00005 before changing any other variable.

requirements: positive aggregate ground-truth, edge, and teacher PSNR versus max-range int7
paired-bootstrap ground-truth lower bound above zero
no source or split regression larger than 0.001 dB
no material degradation concentration in a language or script family

runtime_constraint: The result must retain four packed signed-int7 tensors with one FP16 scale per output channel, exactly the existing artifact layout and byte count.
